correctness.rationale: For equal measurements, reversing every ordered pair yields both \(|z_i-z_j|^2=|y_i-y_j|^2+c\) and equality of the real pairings with the mean coefficients. Double centering gives \(G_z-G_y=(c/2)J\). Since each centered complex configuration has a positive-semidefinite real Gram matrix of rank at most \(2\), \(c>0\) would force rank at least \(n-1\ge3\), while \(c<0\) produces a negative quadratic form on a nonzero vector in \(\ker G_y\cap\mathbf1^\perp\). Hence \(c=0\). Equal Gram matrices give an orthogonal congruence, and the remaining pairing equations plus equal mean norms let the orthogonal extension also map the mean coefficient. This yields exactly the phase-or-conjugate-phase ambiguity. The exact \(n=4\) replay checks \(625\) Gaussian-integer test signals and all \(1864\) measurement collisions without floating point.
